text:
sasha: FYI running into a weird perf + numerical regression after flipping the new kernel-routing heuristic for quantized models. throughput -18% on long-context benchmarks and seeing occasional NaNs in logits. :thinking_face:

maria: ugh. which heuristic? the dynamic shape->int4 path?

sasha: yeah. we started routing requests with avg seq >= 1024 to int4 kernels automatically. thought it would save tokens, but profiler shows a lot more time spent in dequant/reshape paths and some layers producing Inf.

jonathan: can you paste profiler snippet?

sasha: sure, quick capture from local repro (batch_size=4, seq=1536):

```
# perf sample (wall ms)
kernel_dispatcher      12.8
int4_matmul            55.3
dequantize_routine     18.9
kv_cache_expand        9.4
softmax                4.1
final_linear           INF (nan produced)
```

maria: INF at final_linear usually means upstream activations blew up. do we see saturations in layernorm or attention scores?

alex: also, the dequantize path allocates a temp buffer per-token in some hot path we haven't optimized for long sequences yet. that plus int4 -> fp16 upcast overhead might explain throughput drop.

perf-bot: [alert] throughput drop 18% on test-suite/long-context at 2026-03-18T12:03:00Z. regression introduced in 1773430000 (kernel-routing).

sasha: steps I ran to triage:
- repro script: `./bench --model redwood-small --seq 1536 --quant int4 --route auto`
- added `--trace-mem` produced lots of short-lived allocations in `dequantize_routine`
- dumped per-layer max abs activation, observed layer 22, proj_out max ~3.4e38 right before final_linear (overflow)

jonathan: layer 22? that's in the feedforward block after attention. Could be scale mismatch from calibration. Did the int4 calibration run include long-context sequences?

sasha: no, calibration used standard 128/512 sequences. I think the scale factors are undersized when KV cache grows and attention accumulation runs longer.

maria: hypothesis: our current per-tensor scale for weights assumes shorter seq statistical range. with large KV accumulations the intermediate fp16 sums exceed the expected range and then int4 dequantization ramps values up incorrectly, causing overflows. two mitigations: 1) clip activations post-dequant to safe bound, 2) per-channel re-calibration with long-context traces (or smoothquant).

alex: clipping is cheap short-term. try clip at 6.0 or 8.0 and see if NaNs disappear. but that might degrade text quality slightly. we should measure perplexity/regression windows.

sasha: quick test: added a clip in dequant path `x = clamp(x, -CLIP, CLIP)` with CLIP=6.0. Re-ran repro, NaNs gone, throughput -12% (better than -18) but still worse than baseline int8 path.

jonathan: do we have numbers for int8 baseline?

sasha: int8 baseline (same config) throughput 220 tokens/s, int4-without-routing 260 tokens/s, int4-with-routing (broken) 180 tokens/s, int4+clip 195 tokens/s.

maria: suggests overhead is real: dequant+clip cost + thrash in allocator. Longer term: two things — improve kernel selection heuristics to avoid routing to int4 when seq distribution indicates heavy KV churn, and add smoothquant-style per-channel scales during calibration to reduce dynamic range variance.

alex: agree. Also we should change routing rule: don't route to int4 if >25% of requests in the last minute have seq>1024 OR if KV expansion rate > X. That avoids hitting rare tails.

infra-bot: I created infra ticket INFRA-884 to add metrics for `kv_expansion_rate` and `long_seq_fraction` to the routing telemetry.

sasha: provisional plan:
1) revert automatic routing change for production (safe rollback) — alex
2) add temporary clip in dequantize path in canary to prevent NaNs — sasha
3) run smoothquant calibration with long-context traces, per-channel scales, and test int4 again — maria
4) implement routing guarding logic based on `long_seq_fraction` and `kv_expansion_rate` — jonathan
5) benchmark and run quality evals (perplexity + selected prompts) before re-enabling — all

jonathan: for (3) I'd propose this calibration command:
```
./calibrate --model redwood-small --quant int4 --smoothquant --traces traces/long_context/*.npz --per-channel
```
Make sure traces include KV growth patterns (random prompt lengths 256..2048).

maria: also try a hybrid fallback: for layers that have high activation variance (we can detect via cheap statistics during calibration) keep them at int8 or fp16 and quantize rest to int4. That often keeps latency wins without NaN risk.

sasha: ok I'm pushing the clip PR to canary, and will post numbers. Alex will do the rollback. Maria will start calibration job. Jonathan will add routing guard spec. infra-bot already has ticket for metrics.

alex: rollback done — reverted routing change at 1773456900, routing config restored.

perf-bot: [info] canary deploy: clip-dequant PR started at 2026-03-18T12:05:30Z.

sasha: quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely calibration mismatch for int4 scales + allocator thrash in dequant path for long contexts. Fix path: safer routing + per-channel smoothquant + micro-optimizations in dequant buffer reuse.

maria: adding to backlog: smoothquant long-context sweep + per-layer hybrid quant table.

jonathan: can someone dump the layer activation stats to the ticket? I want to check if layernorm residuals are the source vs matmul accumulation.

sasha: will attach logs to INFRA-884 and ENG-RUNTIME-129.

alex: thanks everyone. good catch before it hit prod heavy traffic. :thumbsup:

maria: reassigning owners in the ticket. i'll follow up on calibration results tomorrow. :eyes:
